newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index seesaws in a hold market.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index seesaws in a hold market.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index was down 5.33 points to stand at 3542.98 on Tuesday as investors kept off the market reflecting a wait-and-see attitude predicted by brokers late last week.
Turnover was posted at 25.553 million shillings on 426,837 shares from 29.262 million shillings on 480,895 shares.
"You can't really tell which way the market will go from here because there is no particular direction in the demand and supply, which is why the index is fluctuating," a bourse official said.
A senior broker said there was a lot of speculation on anticipated end-year results expected some time in February.
"Until then it looks like investors will hold on to their shares," he added.
"But everyone is excited because of the general upward movement of prices," another broker said.
There was active trading on the one-hour hold board with Kenya Commercial Bank trading 38,000 shares at 90.50 from 90, and 140,000 shares of East African Packaging at 70 from 72.50.
Foreign demand has sustained the upward movement of Kenya Commercial Bank and brokers predicted that the current trend would continue as there was foreign demand.
Bamburi Cement traded at 40.50 from 39, while Kenya Breweries was unchanged at 52.50.
Despite a lot of negative publicity on the power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting, the share edged to 299 from 280.
The share continues to baffle many investors. The company has announced a revised power rationing programme and predicted a reduction in electricity supply due to a shortfall in rains last year.
"But I think that if they continue to post a good interest income to augment their marginal profits the company will survive," a broker said.
Sasini Tea & Coffee was unchanged at 75 while Kenya Airways eased to 9.30 from 9.80.
